articles.title: 6 DC Comics Moments You Missed This Week (1/28)
articles.summary: January proved to be an eventful month for DC Comics enthusiasts, marked by significant developments in their ongoing series. The intense conflicts of 'DC K.O.' continued, featuring prominent battles, while classic antagonists made surprising reappearances across various storylines. New narratives were also introduced, shaping the future trajectory of the DC Universe. This period highlighted key comic book releases and plot advancements, generating considerable fan engagement.

articles.title: Greenland, NATO, Trump, and the return of great-power geography
articles.summary: Greenland, historically a quiet strategic asset, gained significant global attention following Donald Trump's controversial interest. Its vast natural resources and pivotal geopolitical location in the Arctic make it increasingly important for international defense and resource strategies, sparking renewed discussions among major powers regarding Arctic influence and security.

articles.title: Tractor Supply reins in guidance after weak finish to the year
articles.summary: Tractor Supply's Q4 financial results fell short of internal expectations, despite a 3.3% year-on-year increase in net sales to $3.9 billion. Comparable store sales saw only a marginal rise of 0.3%, and the company experienced a contraction in its gross margin. This performance indicates challenges in meeting growth and profitability targets for the retail giant.

articles.title: Canada and South Korea Pledge to Deepen Auto Manufacturing Ties
articles.summary: Canada and South Korea are exploring plans to bring Korean auto manufacturing to Canada. This effort is part of a broader commitment to deepen industrial cooperation and strengthen economic ties between the two nations. The initiative aims to boost bilateral trade and foster greater collaboration in key sectors, potentially benefiting Canada's automotive industry.

articles.title: Russian ship loitering near transatlantic data cables chased off by Royal Navy attack helicopter — sat within three quarters of a mile of five undersea data cables, including two linking Britain to New York
articles.summary: A Russian cargo vessel recently spent 14 hours anchored less than a mile from five critical transatlantic undersea data cables in British waters. The Royal Navy deployed an attack helicopter to monitor and subsequently chase the vessel away. This incident raises significant concerns regarding the security of vital underwater communication infrastructure and underscores the ongoing importance of maritime surveillance and defence against potential foreign interference.

articles.title: IAF deploys ATC, meteorological team at Baramati after aircraft crash
articles.summary: A chartered aircraft crashed in Baramati, resulting in five fatalities, including Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar. The Indian Air Force (IAF) has deployed resources to the site following the tragic incident. This highlights the critical importance of swift emergency response and multi-agency coordination in national crises, with the IAF's involvement underscoring its role beyond traditional defence operations.

articles.title: Corporate report: Submarine Delivery Agency (SDA): Annual Report and Accounts 2024 to 2025
articles.summary: The Submarine Delivery Agency (SDA), an Executive Agency under the Ministry of Defence, is crucial for maintaining India's naval capabilities. Its primary purpose is to lead a high-performing industrial enterprise focused on delivering advanced submarine capabilities. This ensures the nation's underwater defence readiness and strengthens its strategic maritime presence, vital for national security and strategic advantage.
